transcript.text: Hello, welcome to the On Print Shop tutorial series.
In this video, we'll take you through the essential features and steps to harness the power of the Export Order API within the On Print Shop platform.
The Export Order API in On Print Shop is a powerful tool that can revolutionize your order management process.
By automating exports and offering customization options, you can simplify your workflow and focus on growing your print business.
So let's explore and walk through how to use Export Order API in on print shop.
Go to the admin panel and move to the Orders section from the left side navigation panel.
Then click on the Export API orders.
On this page, you can review the current settings for exporting orders and with the other section, you can manage the orders export process.
Talking about the Settings section, you can verify the present export order settings and an option to manage the same.
Click on the Export API settings to manage the settings.
As you can see, the settings are categorized into three additional sections.
Export API Settings, Hot Folder Settings, and API Services Help.
The Export style setting allows you to set how all orders will be exported.
Select Separate files per order if you want to export all the orders separately or select Single File for all orders If all orders will be exported in a single file.
In the Export file name format, you need to specify the name of the exported file using the below mentioned variables.
Next is the format in which the data will be exported.
You can select from CSV, XML or Jason.
We have a separate section for API Web services where you will have to generate a token.
This token will be used as authentication while using this service.
Then set a format, enter the count for the maximum amount of data to be displayed and provide an IP address.
In the below section of Capture Order Information, there are various pieces of information that you can choose to capture into Excel.
By ticking the checkboxes you can select to get that information.
In the exported Excel file, you can select from Order, product Information, shipping Address, Ship to multiple Addresses, Customer details, and billing address.
Moving to the next tab which is Hot Folder Settings.
With Hot Folder settings you can transfer all your order information into a hot folder.
To do so you can enable the hot folder settings and you can choose the type of folder location.
If you choose the server folder, you need to give the name to that folder.
To create that on the server, select Remove FTP folder and configure your own FTP and the system will create folders in the configured FTP.
Select Printer Wise Remote FTP to create folders based on the printer management system or select Amazon if you want to transfer all the order details to the Cloud storage option.
After selecting the folder location, you need to define the order storage.
The next setting to set is if the job tickets will be moved to the hot folder.
Then select the folder structure if the folder created will have XML, CSVJ, sun files and print ready files in the same folder or in separate folders or it will be managed order wise.
Once done, click on the save button.
The last tab is the API Service Help.
Here you can see the details or what services the API provides.
After all the settings, it is time to export the orders.
Move back to the Export API Orders main screen.
Here select the order range, whether you want a specific order or a less, greater than or less than equals to.
So you can just apply the order range and then select the date range.
Over here, select the order statuses from the drop down and then finally click on the export button to move the order records based on the settings to your offline system.
An Excel file will be downloaded with all the data.
You can open and verify all the details from the file.
Also, you can transfer the data to the hot folder by a manual transfer mode.
Click on the manual transfer.
After selecting the filters, you can see the list of orders within the specified date range and with configured statuses.
You can select the orders from the list and then click on the transfer button to download the file.
And there you have it, you have successfully exported the orders.
If you have any questions, our support executives are here to help.
Just reach out through live chat on onprintshop.com.
Thanks for tuning in.
